title: The Early Elders
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: They are mentioned in [Shabbat 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.64b.15): “The early elders said that she should not paint her eyes,” etc.; in [Nazir 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.53a.5): “some of them used to say”; in Tosefta Ohalot 4:6 and 4:13; and in [Tosefta Yadayim 2:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Yadayim.2.7): “Rabbi Yose ben Durmaskit said: I was with the early elders when they came from Yavneh to Lod.”

In the Sifra, Vayikra, on “Or a soul”: “The early elders used to say: I might think even if he touched,” etc. In the Mekhilta, Beshalach, [Mekhilta, Amalek 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Amalek.2.1), they said: “So this measure goes through all the generations.”

Likewise “elders” without further designation are mentioned in the Mishnah and Gemara, as in Eruvin 8:7, Yoma 1:5, Zevachim 1:3, Yadayim 3:5 and 4:3, Tosefta Ohalot, chapter 18, and the Mekhilta, Beshalach, Massekhta deVayassa; and the elders of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, as in [Eruvin 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.13b.12) and Hyman also cites Beitzah 4a.[^4]
Likewise Hillel and Shammai were called “elders.”

So too Rabban Gamliel the Elder (to distinguish him from Rabban Gamliel his grandson). Likewise they called Rabbi Yose HaGelili, Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehoshua “elders,” as explained in their entries.

Hyman notes that Rabbi always said of Rabbi Yose, “An elder has already ruled.” Hyman suggests that it is always a title for the greatest sage of the generation. The title “elder” is greater than “sage,” in Hyman’s reading of [Taanit 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.16a.9), although the Gemara answers differently.[^3]

notes.text: The Yose ben Durmaskit expansion is distinct from Yehoshua in the named-elders list. Hyman’s always assertion and elder-versus-sage hierarchy remain his interpretation, including his explicit acknowledgment that the Gemara answers otherwise. Collective elders are not merged as a single person.

Shabbat 64b directly preserves the early elders’ prohibition and Akiva’s response. The collective elders are not merged as one individual. Hyman’s always assertion and elder-versus-sage hierarchy remain his interpretation, including his acknowledgment that the Gemara answers differently.

Rabbi Akiva revises the early elders’ adornment ruling in Shabbat. Nazir reports differing opinions among the elders. In Taanit, Abaye says that the preferred speaker is both an elder and a sage. The elders of the two schools in Eruvin are expressly identified by school. The linked Yadayim names Yose ben Durmaskit and the journey from Yavneh to Lod. Oholot 4:4 preserves one of the group’s rulings in the consulted numbering. The linked Amalek passage names them directly. See also [Tosefta Oholot 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Oholot.4.4).

At [Beitzah 4a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.4a.13), Rav follows four elders who rule that a festival and Shabbat have distinct sanctities. [Eruvin 38b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.38b.3) names the four with an alternate fourth name. [Beitzah 4a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.4a.15) records a nearby dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about an egg laid on one of the two days.
